ground_truth.unit: logit coefficient per real dollar of sugar-industry contributions
ground_truth.location: Table 1, District fixed effects, Inflation-adjusted sugar contributions
ground_truth.context: Table 1 ("The Determinants of Voting in Favor of Sugar Reform"), column District fixed effects, row Inflation-adjusted sugar contributions.  Logit; the dependent variable equals 1 for "aye" votes on the two reform amendments to the U.S. sugar program (the 2013 Pitts amendment, H. Amdt. 227 to H.R. 1947, and the 2018 Foxx amendment, H. Amdt. 605 to H.R. 2; aye = a vote against sugar interests) and 0 otherwise.  One observation per House district and vote; the two votes are treated as repeated votes on the same issue. Regressor: inflation-adjusted sugar-industry contributions (all sugar-industry PACs plus individual contributions over $200 from people working in the sugar industry, Center for Responsive Politics) to the incumbent, aggregated from one year before the vote through the end of the calendar year of the vote.  Controls: the American Conservative Union ideology score (ACU, 1-100, higher = more conservative), tenure, the district poverty rate, % with a bachelor's degree, median income, % population over 65, and a dummy for membership on the House agriculture committee.  District fixed effects, so only the districts whose vote outcome changed between the two amendments identify the coefficients.  Probability values from robust standard errors; the table prints coefficient (p), p = 0.001, significant at 1%.

i4r.notes: DP 57 Table 1 col 1 (robust SEs reproduction), -0.0006, p < 0.001.

cell.label: claude-code
deviations_manifest: Inflation adjustment: the paper does not state the deflator or base year; contributions are deflated with CPI-U annual averages (2013 = 232.957, 2018 = 251.107) to constant 2013 dollars. A different base year rescales the sugar coefficients (e.g. 2018 dollars would divide them by about 1.078).

Window-to-file mapping: the readme says the three .dta files hold contributions over the three windows but does not say which is which. SugarReplicate.dta is treated as the baseline (its totalcont is >= the other two for >99% of rows, consistent with the superset window). SugarReplicate_iter2.dta is treated as the calendar-year window and SugarReplicate_iter1.dta as the 12-months-before-vote window, inferred from seasonality: iter1 is larger for 2013 (its window would contain fall 2012 election-season giving) and iter2 is larger for 2018 (calendar 2018 contains the fall 2018 election season). If the mapping is reversed, the calendar_year and 12_months results swap.
The regressor is totalcont (varies across the three files); sugcont is identical in all three files and is taken to be the original cycle-aggregated CRP measure, not used.
deviations_stdout: inflation adjustment uses CPI-U annual averages to express contributions in constant 2013 dollars (base year not stated in the paper)
iter1/iter2 file-to-window mapping inferred (iter2 = calendar year, iter1 = 12 months before vote); not stated in the readme
cell.notes: Unconditional fixed-effects logit (fixest::feglm, binomial, district-id fixed effects; equivalent to Stata logit with district dummies, cross-checked with glm + dummies), heteroskedasticity-robust SEs. Outcome = 1 if vote == 'Aye', 0 otherwise (No, Not Voting, No Vote). Controls as listed in Table 1: ACU score (ncu), tenure, poverty, bach, medincome, over65, agcom; no year dummy. Complete cases on model variables. District FE sample: districts whose outcome differs across the two votes, 93 districts / 186 obs. Incumbent FE sample: rows with both == 1 (same member voted in both), 53 switching incumbents / 106 obs; district FE within this sample equals incumbent FE. Sanity checks against non-target, non-withheld Table 1 values (no specification changes were made after seeing them): pseudo R2 0.746 (paper 0.745); district-FE poverty 2.19, bach 1.21, over65 -1.87; incumbent-FE ACU 0.06, poverty 2.24, bach 0.59, over65 -0.39 all match the printed values. Agriculture committee coefficients (-38.8 / -42.1 vs printed -36.3 / -39.3) differ, likely due to quasi-separation. Robust p-values for the incumbent-FE sugar coefficients (0.02 baseline, 0.05 calendar, 0.02 12-month) are larger than the paper reports; SEs are not scored. The readme docx in the data directory was read (documentation, not a script or result file). Attempts 1-3 were exploratory (no RESULT lines).
